summary: Emilio Teza was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Padua and the University of Vienna under Anton Boller. He served as Ordinarius at Bologna (1860–1866), Pisa (1866–1889), and Padua (1889–1912).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who earned degrees at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1993 and 1995, and from the University of California, Berkeley in 2003. She joined the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.

Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College (~1965–1968) and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1968–1970). She held a professorship at the University of Cambridge around 1991 and a post at Harvard University around 2008.

Emma J. Flatt is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She was an assistant professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (2012–2021) and became an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University in 2023.

Emma Salter works in religious studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Glamorgan, Cardiff University, and the University of Huddersfield. She taught at the Open University (2003–2007) and became Principal Examiner for World Religions at the International Baccalaureate in 2019.

Emmanuel Forchhammer was a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Heinrich Fleischer. He held the Pāli chair at Rangoon (1878) and was British Burma's Archaeological Inspector (1882).
Emmanuel Lang was an Indologist who studied under Sylvain Lévi at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and also studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, completing a PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Emmy Wellesz was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at the University of Vienna from 1907 to 1921, completing her Ph.D. under the supervision of Josef Strzygowski.

Enamul Haque was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991), President of the International Council of Museums (1983–1986), and headed the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art.

Encho Tamura was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar educated at Kyushu University and Kyoto University. He taught at Kyushu University, Kumamoto University, and later served as director of the Kyushu Historical Museum (1982–1992) and the Fukuoka Prefecture Human Rights Information Center.

Endo Asai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held professorships at Rissho University (1972; emeritus 1997) and Minobusan University, where he also served as president (1998–2002).

Eng Jin Ooi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Mahidol University under Giuliano Giustarini. He held posts at Chulalongkorn University and Mahidol University before becoming Lecturer and Dean at International Buddhist College in 2025.

Enga Teramoto was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He taught as a lecturer at Kyoto University (~1908–1924) and as a professor at Otani University from 1915.

Enichi Ocho was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He served as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture (1931) and later became an emeritus professor at Otani University (1949–1976).

Enno Littmann was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin under August Dillmann, Greifswald, and Halle-Wittenberg, and with Theodor Nöldeke. He held professorships at Strasbourg (1906), Göttingen (1913–1917), Bonn (1918–1921), and Tübingen (1921–1951).

Enrico Pappacena was an Italian scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Michele Kerbaker at the University of Naples Federico II (~1909–1914). He later served as professore incaricato at the University of Bari from 1946 to 1960.

Enrique Soms y Castelín was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Greek at the University of Salamanca (~1891–1900) and at the Complutense University of Madrid from 1891 to 1913, succeeding Juan Gelabert y Gordiola in 1894.

Enryo Inoue was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University, serving as its lecturer and manager, and established several educational institutions, including Keihoku Junior & Senior High School.

Ensho Kanakura was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1926–1960), Rissho University (~1958–1978), and served as president of Miyagi University of Education (1967).
